bull.b: A ~64% recurring revenue mix materially improves revenue predictability and reduces dependency on one-off system sales. Over a multi-quarter horizon this supports steadier cash inflows, easier forecasting, and higher lifetime value per customer as the business shifts to SaaS-like recurring contracts.

Mid-50% gross margins indicate the software-heavy product mix can sustain attractive unit economics as the business scales. Higher gross margins provide structural room to cover fixed operating costs, meaning margin expansion can translate into lasting improvements in operating leverage when revenue growth continues.

A sizable government contract vehicle and an expanding product pipeline (GoSecure) create durable addressable opportunities and multi-year revenue potential. Large public-sector channels and new product launches can drive repeatable deployments and upsell, reinforcing scale and market position over quarters.

bear.b: A sequential cash decline to $12.2M, combined with meaningful negative operating and free cash flow, creates ongoing funding risk. Sustaining growth and executing product launches or refinancing requires improved cash generation or external financing, which is a structural constraint until profitability turns.

Persistent EBITDA losses, despite improvement, show the company has not yet achieved scale economics. Continued negative operating profits erode equity and necessitate either sustained cost discipline or revenue acceleration to achieve durable profitability and reduce dilution or financing risk.

Nasdaq minimum bid non-compliance and an adjourned annual meeting signal governance and listing risks that can force corrective corporate actions (reverse split, special financings). These structural overhangs increase execution risk and may constrain strategic flexibility for quarters ahead.
